chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Hajjaj al-Khashshab, from Abu Kahmas al-Haytham ibn Ubayd who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who recites the Quran and then forgets it. I reiterated the question to him three times: Is there any blame upon him for it? He said: No.

key_terms.حَرَج: Constraint, blame, sin — in Islamic jurisprudence, refers to any difficulty or religious violation; the Imam's negation ('la') removes this liability
key_terms.نَسِيَ: Forgot — involuntary forgetting as opposed to deliberate abandonment; the distinction is legally and morally significant in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: Is there a sin for forgetting the Quran after memorizing it?
ai.summary: The narrator Abu Kahmas asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) repeatedly whether a person who memorizes the Quran and subsequently forgets it incurs any sin or blame. The Imam clearly answered in the negative, indicating that forgetting the Quran does not constitute a religious offense. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that unintentional acts beyond one's control do not carry moral culpability.
